name: Slack
description: Read channels, post messages, and search workspace history from your agent.
notes: Both options connect to Slack's official hosted MCP server (https://mcp.slack.com/mcp), which acts as the authorizing user. Slack serves only internal or Slack Marketplace apps that have the MCP server feature enabled, and workspace admins can approve and manage them. The OAuth option is confidential OAuth with the app's client ID and secret (Slack has no dynamic client registration); the token option sends a user token from your own Slack app.

auth.credentialHelp: In your [Slack app](https://api.slack.com/apps), turn on Slack Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server under Agents and add user token scopes such as channels:history, channels:read, chat:write, reactions:write, search:read.public, and users:read ([scopes per tool](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/#oauth-scopes)). Install the app and copy the User OAuth Token from OAuth & Permissions. Sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

installHint: Slack's hosted MCP server needs a Slack app of your own. Create an internal app at api.slack.com/apps, turn on Slack Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server in the Agents section, add the user token scopes for the tools you want, and install it to your workspace (an admin may need to approve it). Then paste the app's User OAuth Token (xoxp-...) below.
